biography:
Paul Vernon, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in the Caterham Academy paddock, hails from the quaint village of Lower Puddleton, Dorset. His journey into motorsport began not on a karting track, but in a field, tearing around on a modified lawnmower his grandfather gifted him. The roar of that engine, the wind in his blonde hair, it was an addiction from the start. He scraped together enough funds working as a barista to enter the Caterham Academy, quickly establishing himself as a force to be reckoned with.

Vernon's early success was punctuated by moments of breathtaking brilliance and equally frustrating errors. A defining moment came at Oulton Park in 2018. After spinning on the first lap, most drivers would have given up. But Vernon, fueled by pure adrenaline and stubbornness, clawed his way back to finish third, overtaking three cars on the final corner. That race solidified his reputation as a showman, a driver who never gives up, no matter the odds.

His career hasn't been without its stumbles. A disastrous 2021 season saw him struggle with reliability issues and on-track incidents, leading some to question his long-term potential. But Vernon has bounced back, refining his skills and tempering his aggression. Now, at 30, he is considered to be at his peak, balancing raw talent with a newfound maturity as he seeks to make a name for himself in higher racing categories.

Currently competing in the Caterham Championship, Vernon is a prominent figure on the grid, known for his daring overtakes and flamboyant personality. He is actively seeking opportunities to advance his career, with aspirations of competing in GT racing.
drivingStyle: Vernon's driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He's a late-braking specialist, often throwing his car into corners with a degree of abandon that leaves spectators gasping. While this approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also leaves him prone to errors. He's working on tire management, a weakness that has cost him valuable points in the past, but his natural instinct is always to attack. Under pressure, Vernon tends to thrive, relishing the challenge of close racing and often pulling off unexpected moves when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: Thorne and Vernon have a long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at Brands Hatch in 2019, where Vernon was deemed to be at fault, resulting in Thorne’s retirement from the race. The two have exchanged heated words on and off the track ever since.

Rossi, a calculated and consistent driver, is the antithesis of Vernon's flamboyant style. Their contrasting approaches often lead to tense battles on the track, with Vernon accusing Rossi of being 'boring' and Rossi dismissing Vernon as 'reckless'.

Blackwood, another rising star in the Caterham scene, shares Vernon's aggressive style, leading to frequent wheel-to-wheel battles and occasional on-track incidents. Their rivalry is fueled by a mutual desire to be the top dog in the series.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of blue socks for every race, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific heavy metal song ('Highway to Hell') right before getting into the car.
Has a habit of talking to his car, affectionately calling it 'Betsy'.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. Out there I'm not looking to make friends, I'm looking to win."
careerHighlight: Winning the Caterham Graduate Championship in 2017 after a season-long battle, securing the title with a dramatic last-lap overtake at Donington Park.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2020 Caterham Championship at Silverstone, costing him a shot at the title due to a mechanical failure.
